key_insight: Maximum convective heat transport is governed by marginal energy stability, not by turbulence intensity, with near-optimal flux arising at the edge of an energy-stability constraint.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a path to high wall heat-transfer rates without sustaining turbulence, potentially enabling more efficient thermal management via designed mean profiles or internal forcing.
method: Marginal energy-stability theory to select admissible mean temperature profiles
Comparison against optimal transport states and rigorous upper bounds
Direct numerical simulations of turbulent flows initialized toward the predicted profiles
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with optimal transport calculations and bounds, predicts Nu ~ 0.0245 Ra^{1/2} at large Ra, and shows turbulent flows relaxing to motionless conductive states while retaining large wall heat flux under internal forcing.
watch_item: The conversion to exact conductive states relies on prescribed internal thermal forcing, so practical implementation may be constrained by how such forcing can be realized in real devices.
paper_title: Optimal heat transport at the edge of energy stability
